results.correct_value: No parking pass or fee is required at either the Upper or Lower Mount Townsend trailhead.
results.evidence: The Forest Service recreation-site pages for both the Upper and Lower Mt. Townsend trailheads state no fees are required; WTA lists Parking Pass/Entry Fee: None; Hiking Project says both trailheads are no-fee. One blog (hikewithkurt) claims a NW Forest Pass is required, against the official pages. access.overnight_permit.where is corrected; bivy[0].permit also hedges toward carrying a pass but bivy is owned by the camping clean-up and is not patched here.

patches.find: a recreation pass is required to park at the national forest trailheads.
patches.replace: no parking pass is needed at either Mount Townsend trailhead.

results.correct_value: Small streams in the first mile or so run early but are often dry by late summer; shallow Windy Lake at Camp Windy is the water source and the last water before the summit.
results.evidence: WTA calls shallow Windy Lake the water source at Camp Windy and says the trail starts beside Townsend Creek. hikewithkurt says the two stream crossings in the first mile are likely dry in late summer and Camp Windy has a reliable water source and is the last water; Gaia GPS lists water at drainages and at Windy Lake. So the approach's claim that the only water near Windy Lake is early-season seeps is the outlier; the 'no dependable creek on the trail' wording is consistent with seasonal streams and is left alone.

patches.find: snowmelt seeps near Windy Lake may run early-season only
patches.replace: the small streams crossed in the first mile or so are often dry by late summer, so shallow Windy Lake by Camp Windy is the last water

results.fact: Extra cost of starting at the Lower Trailhead
results.correct_value: About 2-2.4 extra round-trip miles and roughly 500 ft of extra climbing (not 800 ft).
results.evidence: WTA says the Lower Trailhead is 1.2 miles and 400 ft farther down the valley; The Mountaineers give 1.2 miles and 600 ft; Explore Hood Canal says it adds two miles round trip and 500 ft of gain. All sources put the extra climbing at 400-600 ft, so the pro tip's 800 ft (which double-counts the gain as a round-trip figure) is wrong; the mileage figures (2 vs 2.4) are rounding.

patches.fact: Extra cost of starting at the Lower Trailhead
patches.replace: save about 2.4 mi round trip and roughly 500 ft of extra climbing

Only partner_requirements.experienceLevel mentions scrambling.

results.evidence: access.notes says 'the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply', contradicting access.fees, access.permit, access.parking_pass and access.overnight_permit.what (no overnight permit).
